findings.detail: In a default stdout Scrut block, `{ exec 3>/dev/null; some-command 2>&3; } 3>&1` is accepted without a reason while discarding the child's stderr. The enclosing redirect establishes descriptor 3 as live stdout, but the persistent exec change to that descriptor is forgotten before the next statement. The block-wide uncertainty check considers only exec redirects whose destination descriptor is 1. Propagate persistent descriptor changes between statements, or conservatively withhold live-forwarding exemptions for affected aliases. This recurs in the stream-context class addressed by the inherited-map and explicit-exec fixes; the earlier leading-zero and in/out redirect cases themselves are fixed.
findings.evidence: Static trace: redirected records the enclosing 3>&1 as fds["3"]="stdout". At line 76, each statement receives the same inherited map independently. exec 3>/dev/null changes only its local state and emits no stderr finding. changes_shell_stdout at line 29 ignores descriptor 3, leaving live_scrut true. The following 2>&3 therefore resolves to the stale "stdout" destination and is exempted at lines 61-63. In Bash, the no-command exec redirection persists, so descriptor 3 actually points to /dev/null. Existing saved-alias controls never mutate the alias between statements.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: exec changes to saved descriptors retain stale live destinations

findings.detail: A default stdout Scrut block containing `command builtin exec 1>/dev/null; some-command 2>&1` also bypasses the guard. Bash's builtin prefixes can compose, but the predicate recognizes only exec itself or one command/builtin prefix immediately preceding exec. The persistent stdout redirect is consequently missed, and the later stderr merge is treated as live forwarding despite going to /dev/null. This is a recurring instance of the explicit-exec stream-uncertainty class fixed in a6f57706.
findings.evidence: Static trace: the argument array is ["command","builtin","exec"]. At lines 26-28, the first non-option argument after command is "builtin", so changes_shell_stdout emits nothing. The first statement's stdout-only redirect produces no stderr finding, and its descriptor state is not retained for the next statement. live_scrut remains true at line 115, so the following 2>&1 is exempted. The three exec regression samples cover direct exec and one builtin or command prefix, but no composed prefixes.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: composed builtin prefixes evade exec stream uncertainty
